The curriculum focuses on identifying problems, ideating solutions, and implementing them to create change, whether for financial profit or social betterment.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Segal AmeriCorps Scholarship, Yellow Ribbon Program for Veterans, Tuition Exchange Scholarship

Concentration: Earth System Science, Environmental and Conservation Biology, Environmental Science and Policy, Environmental Engineering
Description: The interdisciplinary environmental science major at Clark University introduces students to the physical, biological, geographical, and policy aspects of the natural environment.  Students will complete core courses and then choose a track to explore in more detail, preparing them for graduate school or careers in fields like ecology, conservation biology, and environmental planning.

Concentration: Earth Systems Science, Environmental and Conservation Biology, Environmental Science and Policy
Description: The Environmental Science minor at Clark University provides an interdisciplinary exploration of the natural environment, covering its physical, biological, geographical, and policy aspects.  Students take six courses that introduce them to the program's three main tracks: earth systems science, environmental and conservation biology, and environmental science and policy.

At Clark University, the Bachelor of Science in Finance program provides a comprehensive understanding of financial markets, investment analysis, and corporate strategy. The curriculum covers capital markets, corporate finance, and emerging trends like sustainable investing and fintech innovation. This program equips students with the skills to analyze financial data, assess investment opportunities, and make sound financial decisions for careers in banking, asset management, and financial consulting.

The finance minor at Clark University covers core finance courses to help students master key financial skills in a relatively compact program. It provides students with the flexibility to complement their majors with different elective courses depending on their career preferences. The program aims to help students gain essential skills for the competitive finance industry.

Concentration: earth system science, human-environment/nature-society, globalization, cities, and development, geographic information science
Description: As a geography major at Clark University, you will use the concepts of place and space to better understand the physical and social processes that shape our planet and to address societal and environmental challenges.  In pursuing a bachelor of arts degree in geography, you will explore why places are different; the economic, political, and cultural systems that connect us locally, regionally, and globally; and how we shape — and in turn are shaped by — our environment.  The Geography major and minor at Clark are set up to give students a broad understanding of physical and human elements that comprise this field of study.
ProgramCategory: Geography##Earth Sciences##Environmental Studies##Geographic Information Systems##Social Sciences
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Presidential Scholarship, Segal AmeriCorps Scholarship

Concentration: Human Environment Geography, Urban Economic Geography, Earth System Science (ESS), Geographic Information Science (GIS)
Description: The Geography minor at Clark University provides students a broad understanding of the physical and human elements of geography.  Students explore the uniqueness of places, the interactions between them, and how place and nature shape our lives and how we shape our environments.  Geographers use the perspectives of place and space to address societal and environmental challenges.

ProgramName: Health, Science & Society, Bachelor of Arts
Description: The Health, Science, and Society major provides an understanding of how biological, environmental, political, and social forces shape individual and societal well-being.  Students learn about the biological and social determinants of health, how socioeconomic structures can create health disparities, and how the human-environment connection influences health.  The curriculum is built on four main perspectives: biomedical science, social determinants of health, data analysis, and ethical considerations.

The Health, Science, and Society minor at Clark University provides an interdisciplinary perspective on health, exploring how biological, environmental, political, and social factors influence individual and community well-being. The curriculum is structured around four key areas: biomedical science, social determinants of health, data analysis, and ethical considerations. This program is designed to give students a strong foundation for various health-related professions by examining health issues from multiple viewpoints.

Concentration: Holocaust and genocide studies, African-American history, the history of the Atlantic world, the history of women and gender
Description: As a history major at Clark University, you will uncover insights and perspectives from the past to better understand the present.  You will collaborate with professors and peers to develop a deep understanding of the past across eras, cultures, and societies.  Through working directly with artifacts, from letters exchanged during the Holocaust to genealogical records, history is brought to life.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Presidential Scholarship, Segal AmeriCorps Scholarship, United World College Scholars Program

Concentration: US History, European History, Global History, Transnational History, Jewish History, History of Human Rights, History of Gender, Political History, History of Violence
Description: The History minor at Clark University offers training in critical thinking, the organization and analysis of information, and clear and concise writing. The program provides a background for various fields including graduate school, teaching, law, government, and journalism. The curriculum is rich and diverse, with courses covering every major geographical area of the world and ranging from political and diplomatic to social, intellectual, and cultural approaches.

ProgramName: International Development and Social Change, Bachelor of Arts
Concentration: Students must complete four courses in a subfield of international development and social change that interests them, but there are no formally named concentrations.
Description: At Clark University, International Development and Social Change (IDSC) majors learn how to bring about positive change by thinking critically, acting collaboratively, and engaging responsibly. Students collaborate with professors and peers to develop a deep understanding of the past across eras, cultures, and societies. The program encourages taking courses across diverse perspectives, including those from the Graduate School of Geography and School of Business, to prepare for work in nonprofit, private, government, and research sectors.
ProgramCategory: International Studies##Social Sciences##Community Development##Global Studies##Social Justice Studies##Sociology
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Grants, Loans, Student Employment

ProgramName: International Development and Social Change Minor
Description: The International Development and Social Change (IDSC) minor at Clark University provides students with a critical understanding of the social, political, economic, and cultural dynamics that shape the world.  Students learn to think critically, act collaboratively, and engage responsibly to bring about positive change in developing nations characterized by economic vulnerability and high poverty levels.  The program emphasizes research and activism, preparing students to tackle the challenges of development in the 21st century.

The marketing major at Clark University equips students with research, communication, and strategic thinking skills to create compelling messages, analyze consumer behavior, and develop innovative marketing strategies. The curriculum covers a range of topics including branding, advertising, market research, digital media, and consumer psychology. This program combines business fundamentals with creative problem-solving, preparing graduates for various careers in the field.

The undergraduate marketing minor at Clark University nurtures innovative and socially responsible leaders, preparing them for success in a wide range of careers such as advertising, digital marketing, and market research. The program provides students with hands-on marketing planning experiences and connects them with businesses and marketing experts. The minor requires the completion of six units of coursework, including three required courses and three units of electives.

Concentration: calculus, algebra, teacher preparation
Description: The Mathematics Education major at Clark University prepares students for a teaching career in middle or secondary education by building content knowledge in mathematics and introducing them to current topics in teacher education. The program, developed in partnership with the Education Department, culminates in a capstone internship with fieldwork in a middle or high school classroom. While it does not directly lead to licensure, it provides early guidance for the Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) program.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Presidential Scholarship, Segal AmeriCorps Scholarship, Clark Global Scholarship Program

Concentration: Pure Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Mathematical Biology, Statistics, Actuarial Science, Teacher Preparation
Description: As a math major at Clark, you can contribute to mathematical knowledge for its own sake (“pure” mathematics), or apply your knowledge of math to solve problems in fields such as chemistry, physics, engineering, economics, and computer science.  Whether you focus on pure or applied mathematics, you will graduate with indispensable skills that lead to careers in fields as diverse as software engineering, finance, actuarial science, and teaching.

Concentration: Actuarial and Financial Mathematics
Description: Clark's mathematics minor provides a solid education in mathematical principles for students who wish to apply mathematics in other fields.  A total of four courses beyond two semesters of Honors Calculus are needed to complete the minor, including two core courses and two electives.  This program is suitable for students who want to complement their major with strong analytical and quantitative skills.

ProgramName: Media, Culture and the Arts, Bachelor of Arts
Description: The interdisciplinary program in media, culture, and the arts (MCA) allows students to study the arts with practitioner-faculty while engaging in their own creative work. The curriculum covers the study of media in their historical, economic, social, and political contexts on various scales. Students take courses that cover a range of cultural theories and historical approaches to media production, alongside hands-on media production courses.
ProgramCategory: Media Design##Art##Communications##Cultural Resources Management##Humanities##Studio Arts##Visual and Performing Arts

Concentration: performance, composition and theory, history and criticism, technology
Description: As a music major at Clark University, you will take foundational courses to build the intellectual and critical tools needed for advanced work. The program offers four tracks of study: performance, composition and theory, history and criticism, and technology, preparing you for a variety of musical fields.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Grants, Loans, Student Employment

Description: The music program at Clark University offers a minor for students with a strong interest in music whose major is in another discipline. Courses are designed to teach students to listen to music intelligently, develop musical perception, and master musical skills. The curriculum provides an acquaintance with music across a broad stylistic, cultural, and historical spectrum.

Concentration: Ethics and Public Policy
Description: The philosophy major at Clark University explores the fundamental questions of life, knowledge, and right and wrong, encouraging students to think beyond easy assumptions and hidden biases. The program helps students develop superior writing and speaking skills while engaging in deep, conceptual analysis of topics ranging from the morality of art to the relationship between science and theology. Students are mentored by faculty with international reputations in a variety of philosophical fields.

Concentration: Ethics and Public Policy
Description: The philosophy minor at Clark University is designed to develop students' intellectual skills and familiarize them with the fundamental methods of philosophical inquiry.  The program helps students cultivate clear and focused writing, analytical and problem-solving skills, and disciplined, effective thinking.  Students pursuing the minor can choose between two specializations, each requiring six courses in philosophy.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Grants, Loans, Student employment

Concentration: Comprehensive Physics, Applied Physics, General Physics
Description: The physics program at Clark University provides a flexible and hands-on approach to exploring the fundamental laws and principles of the universe, from atomic theory to quantum thermodynamics. Students can customize their studies through one of three tracks and engage in research with faculty as early as their first year. The program is designed to prepare students for a variety of careers, including graduate study in physics, engineering, and other sciences, as well as fields like environmental studies, law, and medicine.

Physics is a fundamental science and a key component of a liberal arts education. The minor offers a background in physical principles, the observation of natural processes, and the varied applications of physics.

Concentration: American politics and public policy, comparative politics, international relations
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Political Science at Clark University provides a foundational liberal arts education, allowing students to explore the dynamic subject across three main areas: American politics and public policy, comparative politics, and international relations.  Students investigate a range of issues like civil liberties, human rights, and globalization, with an emphasis on action-based learning through research and internships.  A minimum of 13 courses are required for the major, including foundational classes in research methods and political theory.

Concentration: American politics and public policy, comparative politics, international relations
Description: The political science minor at Clark University requires a minimum of six courses within the department. One must be an introductory course, one must be in either political theory or research methods, and four others can be in any assortment of subfield areas. An internship supervised by a political science faculty member, as well as approved political-science courses taken as part of an accredited study-abroad program, may count toward the minor.

Concentration: peace studies, Holocaust and genocide studies
Description: As a psychology major at Clark University, students explore the human psyche and the connections between thought, feeling, and behavior. The program emphasizes learning how to promote emotional and behavioral health in oneself and others. It is a research-intensive field, requiring at least one lab or research course to integrate diverse cultural perspectives into their work.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Presidential Scholarship, Segal AmeriCorps Scholarship, Yellow Ribbon Program for Veterans, Tuition Exchange Scholarship, Richard Traina Scholarship, Robert Goddard Achievement Scholarship, Jonas Clark Scholarship, Scarlet Award Scholarship, 1887 Scholarship

Description: Clark University's Screen Studies program offers a range of courses on the history, theory, and aesthetics of film, television and new media.  Students have the opportunity to engage in practical, hands-on, collaborative work in digital video production, participating in courses on documentary, fictional narrative, and experimental filmmaking.  The program stresses the importance of a liberal-arts background, as the screen arts are affected by all sectors of contemporary culture and society.
ProgramCategory: Film##Media Design##Visual and Performing Arts##Screenwriting##Film, Television, and Electronic Media

Description: Clark University's Screen Studies minor offers a core of basic and advanced knowledge of the screen arts and media, exploring moving-image media beyond traditional film studies.  The program covers the history, theory, and aesthetics of film, television, and new media, with opportunities for hands-on work in digital video production.  Students are encouraged to explore connections to related fields like visual arts, drama, literature, sociology, psychology, history, and economics.
ProgramCategory: Film##Media Design##Visual and Performing Arts##Film, Television, and Electronic Media

Concentration: law and social control, medicine and community health, social organizations
Description: As a sociology major at Clark University, you will learn to reveal powerful and sometimes hidden social dynamics that impact lives. You'll study broad social processes like global dynamics and social movements, and explore diverse institutions such as law, medicine, family, and religion. This program equips you with conceptual and analytical tools to better understand your own life and the world around you.

Through the study of sociology at Clark University, students acquire the conceptual and analytical tools to enhance their understanding of their own lives and the world in which they live. Students study broad social processes such as global dynamics, stratification, immigration, and social movements, and explore diverse institutions, from law and medicine to family and religion. The sociology minor consists of six courses, including foundational courses in sociological theory and research processes.

The Spanish major at Clark University focuses on building core linguistic and cultural competencies.  Through study abroad, community engagement, and exploration of Spanish-speaking histories, students gain fluency and cross-cultural understanding.  The program prepares students for various fields by developing their ability to use language as a bridge between cultures.
ProgramCategory: Spanish##Hispanic Language & Literature##World Languages and Cultures

Description: To receive a minor in Spanish at Clark University, a student must complete six courses in Spanish literature or culture at the level of SPAN 131/132 or higher. The Language, Literature and Culture Department aims to promote students' competency in other languages while enriching their education through the in-depth study of other cultures. Three of the six required courses must be taken in residence at Clark.

Concentration: Social Praxis in Public Education, Japanese Studies, Music and Technology
Description: The student-designed major at Clark University allows motivated students to create a personalized and rigorous interdisciplinary program of study by integrating courses from several departments.  Students work with a committee of at least three faculty members to conceptualize their major and determine their course of study.  This flexible program prepares students for success in their chosen field through a curriculum tailored to their specific interests and goals.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Presidential Scholarship, Segal AmeriCorps Scholarship, United World College Scholars Program

Description: Studio Art courses at Clark University offer students an opportunity to engage in the study and practice of visual language. The learning of artistic methods and media is embedded in intellectual inquiry and critical analysis, so that the study of Studio Art serves as a meaningful focus of a liberal arts education. Art is seen as a means of communicating human experience; therefore students learn to both read this language and to visually represent their own ideas.

Concentration: acting and directing, technical theater and design, playwriting
Description: Clark University's Theater Arts program offers an intensive study in acting, technical production, and playwriting, encouraging students to explore the various dimensions of theatre arts. The program emphasizes a liberal arts education as integral to the artist's process, providing a foundation for students who may wish to pursue a professional career or simply gain a greater understanding of the field. Students will engage in collaborative storytelling and world-building in a supportive environment with a strong emphasis on live performance.

The Theater Arts minor at Clark University offers students a focused study of theatrical and dramatic arts, combining courses in history, criticism, and theory with practical experience through production involvement. The program is designed for students who wish to pursue acting and/or theatre production while majoring in other areas, providing a broad range of skills to balance their college experience.
ProgramCategory: Theater Arts##Performing Arts##Visual and Performing Arts

ProgramName: Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies, Bachelor of Arts
Description: The Women's and Gender Studies (WGS) major at Clark University provides students with a strong foundation in women's studies and gender analysis.  It introduces them to various disciplinary approaches and helps them develop a specialization within the field.  Courses emphasize the importance of social constructs like gender, sexuality, race, and class in understanding individual and collective experiences.

ProgramName: Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Minor
Description: The Women's and Gender Studies (WGS) minor at Clark University provides students with a foundation in women's studies and gender analysis, introducing them to various disciplinary approaches.  Courses emphasize the importance of social ideas and relationships shaped by gender, ethnicity, race, and class to understand individual and collective experiences.  The program is interdisciplinary, supported by faculty from humanities, social sciences, arts, management, and sciences.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Grants, Loans, Student Employment
